correctness.rationale: For every p and d, simple roots lift uniquely; each distinct repeated root contributes either 0 or p roots. Uniform free coefficient digits give independent repeated-root lift tests by Vandermonde rank since m≤d/2. The monic irreducible Euler product then yields (1), including d=0 and p=2. The polynomial numerator has degree 2p in u with nonzero top coefficient B_p(z)^p, proving sharp stabilization. Derivatives at z=1 give mean one and variance 2(1-1/p), and elementary finite-field factorial-moment counts prove the fixed-degree permutation weak limit and nonconvergent second moment. Independent exact enumeration tested 17 coefficient spaces and 5 conditional spaces.

value.rationale: The object is the complete distribution of local root counts modulo p², a central arithmetic statistic in the 2026 squarefree-values paper and a natural prime-power analogue of a published finite-field counting problem. The formula determines all probabilities in every degree and yields a provably sharp universal stabilization degree 2p, a degree-independent exact variance, and a rare singular-root mechanism for weak convergence without convergence of second moments. It is not merely a finite census or a numerical improvement.
